sources.snippet: Ethology: a social species that reads the human face and body closely and learns by association and by what gets rewarded; the 'dominance/alpha' model is rejected by ESVCE and AVSAB (behaviour problems are not status struggles). Needs (RSPCA five welfare needs): daily exercise and sniffing, social contact, a quiet resting place, predictable routines, things to chew. Stress signs: yawning out of context, lip licking, turning the head away, whale eye, panting at rest, a tucked tail, freezing, displacement scratching. Common mistakes: punishing a growl instead of removing what upsets the dog, hugging and face-to-face contact many dogs only tolerate, leaving a puppy alone for hours without gradual practice, skipping socialisation in the first three months or forcing a frightened puppy (AVSAB puppy socialization, 2008: gradual, never to excessive fear, and it goes on after), using choke, prong or shock tools (AVSAB humane training position, 2021: reward-based methods only; aversive methods are linked to more fear-related aggression).

sources.snippet: Ethology: a solitary hunter that lives in groups only when resources allow; territory and predictability matter more than company; communicates with scent (facial rubbing, scratching, urine marking) and subtle body signals. Needs (ISFM/AAFP environmental needs guidelines): a safe place, several separate key resources (food, water, litter trays, scratching, resting and hiding places: one per cat plus one, in different spots), play that mimics hunting, positive and predictable human contact, respect for the sense of smell. Stress signs: hiding, over-grooming, urinating outside the tray, flattened ears, tail flicking, dilated pupils, eating less, blocking or guarding resources in multi-cat homes. Common mistakes: punishing scratching or marking (they are communication), one litter tray for several cats, trays next to food, introducing a new cat without a gradual scent-first protocol, reading purring as always contentment (cats also purr when in pain or anxious), free-feeding without play.
